fieldDescription: When and how fast the Threat spreads. The incursion begins only after the vanilla abyss story flags fire (finding the Onslaught Mk.I or encountering the Threat).
Master switch. Turning this off freezes the incursion entirely (existing hives remain).

Alternate start trigger: a player colony reaching the size below wakes the swarm even without touching the abyss questline - whichever comes first. A maxed colony is exactly the concentration of technology the Threat exists to destroy.
Player colony size that wakes the swarm (6 = vanilla max via natural growth).
How often the incursion clock advances. Higher = slower everything.
How many fringe systems are seeded when the incursion begins.
Days for a seeded system to grow a Fabrication Hive.
Days for a hive system to saturate and begin launching strikes.
Per-tick chance of spreading to a new system, multiplied by the number of live hives. Killing hives directly slows this.
Upper bound on the per-tick spread chance.
Hard cap on simultaneously infested systems.
Phase 1: fringe expansion (no attacks). Phase 2: strikes at outlying colonies. Phase 3: core worlds in reach.
Days after the incursion starts before strikes on outlying colonies can begin.
Minimum live hives before phase 2 can begin.
If on, phase 3 eventually puts the core worlds (size 6+ colonies) in reach.
Days after the incursion starts before core-world strikes can begin.
Minimum live hives before phase 3 can begin.
Saturated hive systems launch incursion fleets at inhabited worlds - real fleets you can intercept and fight alongside the defenders.
Minimum days between strikes launched from any one saturated system.
Sector-wide cap on simultaneous Threat strikes.
How far from a saturated system strikes can reach.
Combined fleet strength of a strike (the Remnant Retribution strike uses 50 as its base, for comparison).
Minimum days between strikes that target YOUR colonies specifically. NPC worlds get no such mercy.
Systems defended by a live Remnant Nexus resist infestation - the swarm must win a war of machines first. Purging the Remnant yourself clears the Threat's path.
If on, the spread cannot claim a system with a live Remnant Nexus without first destroying it in a machine war.
Per-attempt chance the swarm destroys a defending Remnant Nexus. Failures are retried on later spread attempts.
Tools for testing. Effects apply on the next incursion clock check (about half a day of game time).
Logs spread/hive/strike events to starsector.log (prefix [ThreatInc]).
Starts the incursion immediately, skipping the story-flag trigger. Turn off again afterward.
Runs the entire incursion 10x faster for testing: tick cadence, stage durations, strike intervals, and phase delays.

Grants the Onslaught Mk.I sensor modifications (10x detection range vs Threat fleets) that a normal playthrough earns from the abyss quest. Without them Threat fleets are seen at one tenth normal range. Note: having the sensor mods also counts as the incursion's start trigger, as in vanilla.
